description.html: Dragon stone, also known as Ohko stone, is one of the most popular rocks in aquascaping. It is porous, with deep hollows and small holes that resemble dragon skin, and its color ranges from yellow-orange to brown. A 1 kg pack contains irregularly shaped pieces, so every arrangement looks different.

In an aquarium it is used for hardscape, the rock formations that form the backbone of an aquascape. Mosses and plants that grow on rock attach easily to its rough surface, and the gaps between stones provide shelter for fish and shrimp. In a terrarium it serves as a natural decoration, a climbing surface and a base for hides.

Dragon stone often carries dust and clay residue in its pores. Before use, rinse the stones well under running water and brush them, and scrape off harder deposits with a pointed tool. When building larger formations, place the bigger pieces directly on the bottom, before the substrate, so they do not shift or collapse.
Sources disagree on whether this stone affects water parameters, so in aquariums with soft, acidic water, check pH and KH from time to time after setting it up.
